examples.en: My younger sibling tattled on me to Mom.
Because of the snitching, the friends drifted apart.
Please don't go telling on me to the teacher.

examples.ko: 이건 고자질이 아니라 꼭 알려야 하는 일이에요.
examples.en: This isn't tattling; it's something that must be reported.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 고자질을 많이 해서 혼났어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I got scolded for tattling a lot.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 고자질을 잘해서 인기가 없어요.
examples.en: That friend tattles a lot, so he's not popular.

explain: 남의 잘못을 윗사람에게 몰래 말하는 나쁜 느낌의 말이라서 주로 아이들 사이에서 많이 나와요. 꼭 알려야 하는 일은 '신고'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: It has a negative tone, and is heard a lot among children. When something truly must be reported, people use '신고' instead.

examples.ko: 그런 바보짓은 이제 다시 안 할 거예요.
examples.en: I won't do such a foolish thing ever again.
I was angry and did something stupid on the spur of the moment.
Playing games all night before the exam was a foolish thing to do.

examples.ko: 그 사람 때문에 바보짓까지 하게 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of that person, I even ended up doing silly things.

examples.ko: 괜히 바보짓 하지 말고 한 번 더 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't do anything foolish, think once more.

examples.ko: 그때 한 바보짓이 아직도 생각나서 창피해요.
examples.en: I still remember the foolish thing I did back then, and I'm embarrassed.

explain: '바보 같은 짓'을 줄인 느낌으로, 자기 행동을 후회하며 말할 때 자주 써요. '짓'은 행동을 낮춰 말하는 말이라서, 남의 행동에 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It feels like a shortened '바보 같은 짓' and is often used when regretting your own actions. Since '짓' belittles an action, using it about someone else's behavior can sound rude.

examples.en: Two kids bumped heads while running.

examples.ko: 축구 선수가 상대에게 박치기를 해서 퇴장당했어요.
examples.en: The soccer player head-butted an opponent and was sent off.
A head-butt is a foul in wrestling.

examples.ko: 동생이 갑자기 내 배를 박치기로 들이받았어요.
examples.en: My little brother suddenly head-butted my stomach.
We almost bumped heads in front of the door.
The baby bumped his head on the corner of the bed while playing.

explain: '박치기하다'로 동사처럼도 써요. 일부러 머리로 들이받을 때뿐 아니라 실수로 머리끼리 부딪칠 때도 써요. 사고 상황을 말할 때는 '머리를 부딪치다'가 더 차분한 말이고, '박치기'는 어린이 말투 같은 가벼운 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: It is also used as a verb, '박치기하다'. It covers deliberate head-butts and accidental head bumps. For an accident, '머리를 부딪치다' sounds calmer; '박치기' has a light, childlike feel.

en: round and round; with a smile

examples.en: The ride spins round and round.
The child is spinning round and round on the spot.
A bird is circling in the sky.
I spun too much and my head is spinning.
The laundry spins round and round inside the washing machine.

examples.ko: 길을 못 찾아서 같은 곳을 빙글빙글 돌았어요.
examples.en: I couldn't find the way and went around the same place in circles.

explain: '빙글빙글'은 둥글게 계속 도는 모양을 나타내요. '돌다'와 함께 쓰고, 어지러울 때는 '머리가 빙글빙글 돌아요'라고 해요. 또 '빙글빙글 웃다'처럼 소리 없이 부드럽게 웃는 모양도 나타내요. 비슷한 '뱅글뱅글'은 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: '빙글빙글' shows something turning in a continuous circle. It goes with '돌다', and for dizziness you say '머리가 빙글빙글 돌아요'. It also describes a soft, silent smile, as in '빙글빙글 웃다'. The similar '뱅글뱅글' feels smaller and lighter.

examples.ko: 어영부영 하다 보니 벌써 한 해가 다 갔어요.
examples.en: Before I knew it, the whole year was already gone.

examples.ko: 어영부영 시간만 보내지 말고 계획을 세워요.
examples.en: Don't just let time slip by; make a plan.

examples.ko: 시험 준비를 어영부영하다가 점수가 낮게 나왔어요.
examples.en: I prepared for the exam half-heartedly, and my score came out low.

examples.ko: 그 문제를 어영부영 넘어가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't just brush that problem aside.

examples.ko: 어영부영 대답하지 말고 분명하게 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't answer vaguely; please say it clearly.
I drifted through the days, and the vacation was over.

explain: 뚜렷한 계획 없이 대충 시간을 보내거나, 일을 얼버무려 넘길 때 써요. 대체로 부정적이고 '어영부영 하루가 갔어요'처럼 아쉬움이 담겨요. '얼렁뚱땅'은 눈속임으로 슬쩍 넘기는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is used when you spend time aimlessly without a clear plan, or gloss over a matter. It is usually negative and carries regret, as in '어영부영 하루가 갔어요'. '얼렁뚱땅' has a stronger feeling of slyly getting past something by trickery.

examples.en: My headaches have become frequent lately, so I went to the hospital.
As overtime became more frequent, I lost time to exercise.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날이 잦아지는 걸 보니 장마가 시작되나 봐요.
examples.en: Rainy days are getting more frequent, so the rainy season must be starting.
We were in touch often for a while, but lately it has become rare again.

examples.ko: 회의가 잦아지지 않도록 일정을 미리 정해요.
examples.en: We set the schedule in advance so meetings don't become too frequent.
The more frequent the earthquakes get, the more anxious I become.

explain: 어떤 일이 전보다 자주 일어나게 될 때 써요. 반대는 '뜸해지다'나 '드물어지다'예요. 비슷하게 생긴 '잦아들다'는 소리나 비바람이 약해진다는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: Used when something starts to happen more often than before. The opposite is '뜸해지다' or '드물어지다'. Don't confuse it with the similar-looking '잦아들다', which is a different word meaning sounds or storms subside.

examples.en: The elevator suddenly stopped.

examples.ko: 비밀번호를 세 번 틀리면 계정이 정지돼요.
examples.en: If you get the password wrong three times, the account is suspended.
I captured the frozen screen.

examples.ko: 공사 때문에 오전에는 공장 기계가 정지될 거예요.
examples.en: The factory machines will be stopped in the morning because of the construction.
When the car stopped, people got off.
My driver's license was suspended, so I can't drive.

explain: '멈추다'와 달리 '정지되다'는 기계, 계정, 면허처럼 '누가 멈추게 한' 것에 주로 써요. 사람이 걷다가 멈출 때는 '멈추다', '서다'를 써요. 기계·서비스의 '일시 정지'는 '일시 정지돼요'로 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike 멈추다, 정지되다 mostly describes machines, accounts or licenses that were stopped by something. For a person stopping while walking, use 멈추다 or 서다. For machines and services, '일시 정지되다' means 'temporarily suspended'.

en: take one's anger out on; vent anger

examples.en: Please do not take your anger out on me.
He took out his anger by throwing things.

examples.ko: 스트레스 받는다고 가족에게 화풀이하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take your stress out on your family.
Some of my friends vent their anger through exercise.
If I am upset, I will go to karaoke and blow off steam.
Why are you taking it out on me?

explain: '~에게/한테 화풀이하다'처럼 대상을 말해요. 그 사람이 화난 이유가 아닌데 터뜨린다는 느낌이에요. '화를 풀다'는 마음을 가라앉힌다는 좋은 뜻도 되지만, '화풀이하다'는 남에게 터뜨리는 나쁜 느낌이에요.
explain_en: The target takes '~에게/한테': '~에게 화풀이하다'. It implies the person is not the reason for the anger. '화를 풀다' can mean calming down in a good way, but '화풀이하다' is negative, letting it out on others.
